details:
Live captioning and translation tools for VRChat (VRCT, Whispering Tiger and others) can only capture the mixed desktop audio. They cannot tell one speaker from another, and a world's video player gets mixed in with everyone's voices. Continuous video audio delays or garbles the captions of the people actually talking to you. This matters most to deaf and hard-of-hearing players, and to players talking across languages.

VRChat already knows who is talking and where their voice comes from. Please let a local OSC app receive that, opt-in:

- /voice/players/<n>/talking (bool): the player's voice is active.

- /voice/players/<n>/loudness (float, 0–1): the voice level as you hear it, after distance falloff.

- /voice/players/<n>/direction (float, −180 to 180): the voice's direction relative to your head.

- /world/media/playing (bool): a world video or audio player is playing.

<n> is a per-instance index, so no names or IDs are needed.

Safeguards:

- Off by default. Turning it on is a setting in the OSC menu.

- Sent only to apps on the same machine (OSCQuery, as /tracking is today).

- Only players you can currently hear: muted, blocked and out-of-range players are left out.

- No audio is sent, only activity.

Related: "Player Voice variables for Udon (isTalking, loudness, viseme)" asks for the same signals inside worlds. This request is for the OSC side, so that accessibility tools outside the game can use them.
title: OSC output of nearby players' voice activity (who is talking, and from where) for captioning and translation tools
